summary: Helga Uebach was a Tibetologist who earned her Ph.D. at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1961–1967). In 1964, she served as a wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Hellmut Wilhelm worked in Sinology, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1928–1932). He later served as Professor of Chinese Studies and Associate Director of the Far Eastern Institute at the University of Washington (~1948–1973).
Helmer Smith was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held academic posts at Lund University from ~1921 to 1936 and at Uppsala University from ~1936 to 1947.
Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1968–1973) and held a post as Dr. at the University of Bonn (attested 1991–2010).

Helmut Hoffmann was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied under Heinrich Lüders, Giuseppe Tucci, and Ferdinand Diederich Lessing, later holding professorships at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1948) and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1989–2014) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1989–2014), and was director of the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Helmut Rix specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Würzburg (~1946–1950). He held posts at the University of Regensburg (~1968–1978) and the University of Freiburg (~1978–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held a professorship at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hermann Jacobi and Wanczura, and held posts as Privatdozent at Bonn and Berlin, followed by chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).
Hendrik Kern was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and under Albrecht Weber, and served as a professor at Leiden University from 1865 to 1903.

Heng Sure is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, where he earned a PhD under supervisors Ronald Y. Nakasone and Edmond Yee, and also studied under Hsuan Hua.
Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University from ~1985 to 1997 and held a post there around 1998.

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1961–1973). He served as dean of the Faculty of Arts at Utrecht (1980–1986) and professor at Leiden University (1992–2002).
Henri Gaidoz was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865.

Henri Maspero specialized in Sinology, religious studies, and linguistics, studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and ENLOV. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, as professor at the Collège de France (1920–1945), and at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930).

Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the University of Liège, Ghent University, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1930).
Henrik Samuel Nyberg was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908 and later held a post there from ~1919 to 1956.

Henry Chung-hung Shiu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto, studying under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, Julia Ching, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Clarke Warren was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Harvard Oriental Series. He earned his B.A. at Harvard University (~1875–1879) and studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman at Johns Hopkins University in 1879.

Henry George Keene was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served in the East India Company (~1798–1811) and was Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (~1824–1834).
